issues.title: SettingsTextFormatter missing @MainActor annotation
issues.description: The rule requires that classes interacting with UIKit or performing UI updates must be marked with @MainActor annotation. The SettingsTextFormatter class formats text for UI display in settings screens but lacks the @MainActor annotation.
issues.rule_name: UI-Related Code Must Be Annotated with @MainActor

issues.title: Incorrect localized string reference in SettingsTextFormatter
issues.description: The formatStudiesText method references strings.detailTextStudies instead of strings.detailTextStudiesV2. This causes the formatter to display the old v1 Studies message ('%@ may install and run studies from time to time.') instead of the new v148 message ('%@ randomly selects users to test features, which improves quality for everyone.') that was added in this PR. The helper class was clearly intended to format the new v148 strings based on the PR context, but uses the wrong string constant.

issues.title: Inconsistent format specifier documentation in RolloutsSettingMessage comment
issues.description: The comment for RolloutsSettingMessage incorrectly documents the format specifier as '%1$@' (positional format) while the actual value string uses '%@' (simple format). This mismatch creates confusion for localization teams and could lead to incorrect translations, as translators may attempt to use positional formatting based on the comment when the string implementation doesn't support it. The comment should match the actual format specifier used in the value field.

issues.title: Linter exclusion points to wrong message key version
issues.description: The linter configuration exclusion was updated to reference 'Settings.Studies.Message.v148' but the original PR added this key to exclude quotes validation for the v136 message. Since the PR adds new v148 strings with similar content containing quotes, the exclusion should have remained as v136 to maintain the existing exclusion, or both versions should be excluded. This change will cause the linter to fail validation on the v136 string that legitimately needs the exclusion, while potentially missing issues in the new v148 string.

issues.title: SettingsTextFormatter class missing final keyword
issues.description: The newly added SettingsTextFormatter class violates repository Rule #12 from AGENTS.md, which requires classes that are not designed for subclassing to be marked with the 'final' keyword. This helper class is clearly not intended for inheritance (it has a private initializer and is a simple utility class), but lacks the final modifier. This prevents compiler optimizations and fails to communicate design intent explicitly, violating an explicit compliance rule added in this same PR.

issues.title: SettingsTextFormatter and its methods lack explicit access control
issues.description: Rule requires explicit access control modifiers. The new nested class and its members use default (implicit) access levels (`class`, `static let shared`, and `func` declarations have no explicit `internal`/`private`/`public`).
issues.rule_name: Properties and Methods Must Have Appropriate Access Control

issues.title: SettingsTextFormatter should be marked final
issues.description: The helper singleton class is not designed for inheritance but is declared as a non-final class. Per the rule, such classes must be marked `final` to prevent unintended subclassing and enable compiler optimizations.
issues.rule_name: Classes That Should Not Be Subclassed Must Be Marked Final

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #31198 - EXP-5874 Add strings for Rollouts toggle and update Studies strings

structured_output.summary:
This PR adds the v148 strings for splitting the Studies toggle into a "Studies" toggle and a "Rollouts" toggle. On Firefox iOS that means six new `MZLocalizedString` entries in `Shared/Strings.swift`, plus hand-added copies in the en-CA and en-GB `Settings.strings` files. It also adds a quotes-linter exclusion. On the Focus side, `UIConstants.strings` gets parallel V2/Rollouts strings and a new `SettingsTextFormatter` helper.

The Firefox string additions look fine. The Focus changes have a real bug and go beyond what the PR says it does: the new `SettingsTextFormatter.formatStudiesText` formats the old `detailTextStudies` string instead of the new `detailTextStudiesV2`, so the new Studies copy would never appear. The PR also adds `detailTextSendUsageDataV2`, which nobody asked for and which repeats the existing string word for word. Smaller problems: the Rollouts message comment uses `%1$@` while the string uses `%@`, the quotes-linter exclusion targets a string that has no quotes in it, and the en-CA/en-GB locale files were edited by hand.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The new Focus formatter uses the old v1 Studies string, so whoever wires it up will show outdated copy. The PR also adds a duplicate, unexplained Send Usage Data V2 string and a quotes-linter exclusion with nothing to exclude. These should be fixed or removed before merge.

architecture.overview:
Firefox iOS declares UI strings in `Shared/Strings.swift` with `MZLocalizedString(key:tableName:value:comment:)`. Those keys are exported to an XLIFF file for Pontoon (Mozilla's translation platform) and checked by the l10n linter using `.github/l10n/linter_config_ios.json`. Translated `*.lproj/*.strings` files then come back through the l10n import. Focus iOS keeps its strings as `NSLocalizedString` constants in `UIConstants.strings`, and `SettingsViewController` formats them with `AppInfo.productName`.

This PR adds v148 keys for a new Studies copy and a new Rollouts toggle (title, message, learn-more) on both apps. It seeds en-CA/en-GB translations by hand and adds a linter exclusion. On Focus it also adds a `UIConstants.SettingsTextFormatter` singleton that wraps `String(format:)` for the studies and rollouts descriptions. Nothing calls the new strings yet; the follow-up PR #30988 is expected to wire them up.
steps: Start in `firefox-ios/Shared/Strings.swift` around line 6232: six new v148 keys in the `Settings` table, next to the existing v136 Studies strings that `AppSettingsTableViewController` still uses.
Look at the hand-added en-CA/en-GB `Settings.strings` entries. Normally these files come from the l10n import, not from code PRs.
Check `.github/l10n/linter_config_ios.json`, which adds a quotes exclusion for `Settings.Studies.Message.v148`.
Move to Focus `UIConstants.strings` (lines 202-209): new V2 Studies, Rollouts, and SendUsageData V2 constants.
Finish with the new `UIConstants.SettingsTextFormatter` (lines 417-430), which formats the description strings with an app name and is not called anywhere yet.

findings.title: SettingsTextFormatter.formatStudiesText uses the old v1 Studies string
findings.fixPrompt: In `focus-ios/Blockzilla/UIComponents/UIConstants.swift` lines 417-430, `SettingsTextFormatter.formatStudiesText` formats the old `strings.detailTextStudies` instead of the new `strings.detailTextStudiesV2` added in this PR, so the new Studies description would never appear. Change it to use `detailTextStudiesV2`. Better still, since this PR is meant to only add strings and nothing calls the formatter, remove the `SettingsTextFormatter` class entirely and let the follow-up UI PR format the strings inline, as `SettingsViewController.swift:127` already does.

findings.title: Unrequested detailTextSendUsageDataV2 duplicates the existing string
findings.fixPrompt: In `focus-ios/Blockzilla/UIComponents/UIConstants.swift` line 203, remove `detailTextSendUsageDataV2`. It repeats `detailTextSendUsageData` word for word (same value and comment), nothing uses it, and it falls outside this PR's Studies/Rollouts scope. A new key with identical text just makes translators redo the same sentence.

findings.title: Rollouts message comment says %1$@ but the string uses %@
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/Shared/Strings.swift` line 6261, the comment for `RolloutsSettingMessage` says `%1$@`, but the value uses `%@`. Change the comment to say `%@`, matching the value, the sibling `StudiesSettingMessageV3` comment, and the en-CA/en-GB `.strings` comments.

findings.title: Quotes-linter exclusion targets a string with no quotes
findings.fixPrompt: In `.github/l10n/linter_config_ios.json` lines 7-11, the PR adds a quotes-linter exclusion for `firefox-ios.xliff:Settings.Studies.Message.v148`, but that string (defined in `firefox-ios/Shared/Strings.swift` around line 6242) has no quote characters. Revert the exclusions array to `[]` unless the linter actually flags this key. If it does, explain in the PR why.

findings.title: en-CA/en-GB Settings.strings edited by hand
findings.fixPrompt: Revert the hand-added v148 entries in `firefox-ios/Shared/Supporting Files/en-CA.lproj/Settings.strings` and `en-GB.lproj/Settings.strings`, including the en-GB trailing-newline change. These files come from the l10n import, and the English fallback values in `firefox-ios/Shared/Strings.swift` already cover these keys until translations land.

findings.title: Firefox strings follow the versioned-key convention
findings.body: The new keys in ::file{file="firefox-ios/Shared/Strings.swift"} use new `.v148` keys instead of changing the text of the existing v136 keys. That's the correct l10n practice, because the old translations stay valid until the UI switches over. The placeholder comments also explain what `%@` stands for, which helps translators.
